title: Submersible Sewage Pump

introduction.definition: A submersible sewage pump is a close-coupled motor-pump unit designed to run submerged in a wet well, pumping raw sewage and storm water with solids and fibres. It uses a non-clog impeller with large free passage, tandem mechanical seals with an oil chamber, and usually installs on a guide-rail and duckfoot so it can be lifted out without entering the well.
key_points: Tandem seals with oil chamber and leakage sensor
Motor cooled by surrounding liquid or a cooling jacket
introduction.summary: A centrifugal pump and its sealed electric motor form one unit that sits on the floor of a sewage wet well, fully submerged. Raw sewage enters through the bottom inlet into a two-channel non-clog impeller whose wide passages pass solids and fibres. Two mechanical seals with an oil chamber between them keep water out of the motor. The pump slides down two guide rails and couples automatically to the duckfoot bend on the floor, so it can be lifted out for service without entering the well.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flat to moderately steep curve; efficiency lower than clean-water pumps because of the large free passage.

parts.name: Volute Casing
parts.function: Collects flow leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure in a spiral passage of increasing area, then discharges through a diffuser nozzle.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, carbon steel, stainless steel (CF8M), duplex.

parts.name: Two-Channel Non-Clog Impeller
parts.function: Pumps sewage containing solids and rags with minimum clogging.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, hardened high-chrome iron for grit.

parts.name: Motor Housing & Oil Chamber
parts.function: Watertight housing for the motor; oil chamber between the two seals; cable entry and lifting points.

parts.name: Lifting Handle
parts.function: Point for lifting the pump out along the rails.

parts.name: Stator
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Converts the rotating field into shaft torque (squirrel-cage induction rotor).
parts.material: Electrical steel, die-cast aluminium or copper.

parts.name: Motor Bearings
parts.function: Support the motor rotor at drive and non-drive ends.

parts.name: Tandem Mechanical Seals (in Oil Chamber)
parts.function: Two mechanical seals in series: the lower seal faces sewage, the upper seal faces the motor; oil between them lubricates and acts as barrier.
parts.material: Silicon carbide, tungsten carbide, carbon, ceramic.

parts.name: Guide Claw & Sealing Flange
parts.function: Slides on the guide rails and seals the pump discharge against the duckfoot flange by the pump weight.

parts.name: Duckfoot Bend (Auto-Coupling Base) & Riser
parts.function: Floor-mounted discharge bend that receives the pump and turns the flow up into the discharge riser.

parts.name: Guide Rails (2 in pipe)
parts.function: Guide the pump down to the duckfoot and back up for service.

parts.name: Lifting Chain & Power Cable
parts.function: Supplies power from the control panel to the motor; chain lifts the pump.

parts.name: Float Level Switch
parts.function: Starts and stops the pump at set levels and gives high-level alarm.

foundation: Duckfoot anchored to the wet-well floor; guide rails plumb and fixed to the upper bracket.
alignment: Guide claw must engage the rails freely.
piping: Riser and check valve sized for self-cleansing velocity (≈ 0.7–1 m/s in rising mains, verify local standards).
commissioning: Set float levels for start/stop/alarm; limit starts per hour.

routine.task: Check current, run hours and starts per hour.

periodic.task: Check oil chamber for water (seal leakage).
Lift the pump and clean rags from the impeller.

overhaul.task: Replace seals, bearings and the impeller/wear plate as needed.

lubrication: Sealed-for-life bearings; oil chamber refill with specified oil.

video_tutorials.title: Submersible Sewage Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Submersible Sewage Pump.
A submersible sewage pump is a close-coupled motor-pump unit designed to run submerged in a wet well, pumping raw sewage and storm water with solids and fibres.
It uses a non-clog impeller with large free passage, tandem mechanical seals with an oil chamber, and usually installs on a guide-rail and duckfoot so it can be lifted out without entering the well.
Typical applications include municipal sewage lift stations; storm-water and drainage pumping; industrial effluent and sludge transfer; building drainage sumps.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Volute Casing, Two-Channel Non-Clog Impeller, Rotor & Shaft.

video_tutorials.title: Submersible Sewage Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Submersible Sewage Pump.
Check current, run hours and starts per hour.
Check oil chamber for water (seal leakage).
Lift the pump and clean rags from the impeller.
Replace seals, bearings and the impeller/wear plate as needed.
Watch for clogging: high current then low flow. Common cause: rags and wipes.
Watch for seal leakage: moisture alarm. Common cause: worn seals, abrasive grit.
Watch for motor overheating: thermal trips. Common cause: low level (motor uncovered), excessive starts.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: What does "free passage" of a sewage impeller mean?
options: The largest sphere that can pass through the impeller
questions.explanation: Key selection value for solids handling.

questions.question: How does the pump connect to the discharge pipe?
options: It slides down guide rails and seals on the duckfoot by its own weight

questions.question: Why use tandem seals with an oil chamber?
options: To give two barriers between sewage and the motor
questions.explanation: The oil chamber also allows leak detection.
